sources.title: How to Run Muse Glimmer 30B Locally for AI Coding - DataCamp
sources.snippet: How to Run Muse Glimmer 30B Locally for AI Coding Run Meta's Muse Glimmer local agentic model using llama.cpp, dynamic quantization, DFlash speculative decoding, vision support, and OpenCode to run a fast, private, and low-cost AI coding agent.

sources.title: How to Run Muse Glimmer 30B Locally: Ollama, llama.cpp, and vLLM
sources.snippet: Meta released Muse Glimmer on August 10, 2026 under Apache 2.0. It is a 30B dense multimodal model built specifically for agent loops that run on your own hardware — the kind that stay resident all day, call tools, and never send a token to an API.

sources.title: Muse Glimmer - Meta
sources.snippet: An open 30B model for always-on local agents. Runs on a single GPU, Apache 2.0 licensed. Tuned for tool use, long tasks, and failure recovery.

sources.title: Model API | Muse Glimmer - dev.meta.ai
sources.snippet: Muse Glimmer is Meta's 30-billion-parameter open-source multimodal model, distilled from Muse Spark and built for local agentic workflows. Run it on your own hardware through supported runtimes. sources.title: meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B | vLLM Recipes
sources.snippet: Dense 29.6B vision-language model with a ViT-G/14 perception encoder and 128K context, distilled from Muse Spark for local agentic use. Emits channel-scoped reasoning and XML-style ATEM tool calls rather than JSON, so it needs the dedicated `muse_glimmer` tool-call and reasoning parsers.
